section_title: Huntington's Disease and Striatal SST Interneurons
thesis: The textbook claim that striatal SST/NPY/NOS interneurons are spared in Huntington's disease rests on peptide concentrations measured in atrophic tissue, and the primary authors described relative, not absolute, preservation. Transcript measurements in the same region fall, model studies report 8-14% losses, cortical SST populations are reduced, and the spared cells carry abundant aggregates - so sparing is a statement about relative cell death, not about functional integrity.
scope_notes: HD: why striatal SST/NPY/NOS interneurons are relatively spared, and evidence that they are nonetheless dysfunctional.

findings.claim: Optogenetic silencing of somatostatin-expressing striatal interneurons reduced spontaneous IPSC frequency in spiny projection neurons of Q175 HD mice but not in wild-types, indicating a disproportionate SOM-interneuron contribution to SPN inhibition in HD.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Thus, the overall change in sIPSC frequency during inhibition of SOM-expressing interneurons for all recorded SPNs was greater in Q175s than in WTs (−15.14 ± 5.0% in Q175 SPNs vs. 1.94 ± 2.7%; t(30) = 3.24, p = 0.003; Figure 4H).
findings.evidence: Optogenetic (halorhodopsin/ChR2) interrogation of SOM- and PV-interneuron inputs onto SPNs with whole-cell recordings in Q175 knock-in mice across ages.
findings.effect_size: sIPSC frequency change during SOM-interneuron inhibition: -15.14 +/- 5.0% in Q175 SPNs vs 1.94 +/- 2.7% in WT
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Thus, the overall change in sIPSC frequency during inhibition of SOM-expressing interneurons for all recorded SPNs was greater in Q175s than in WTs (−15.14 ± 5.0% in Q175 SPNs vs. 1.94 ± 2.7%; t(30) = 3.24, p = 0.003; Figure 4H).
findings.study_system: Q175 (zQ175) heterozygous knock-in mouse model of HD; striatal SPN whole-cell recordings

findings.claim: Striatal somatostatin interneuron numbers were unchanged in BACHD mice while parvalbumin interneurons were significantly reduced, supporting selective sparing of the SOM/NPY/NOS population.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We found that the number of SOM interneurons was not significantly reduced in BACHD mice (BACHD- 28.1 ± 4.0) when compared to wild-type mice (WT- 28.8 ± 2.7, p = 0.4957; Figure 3C).
findings.evidence: Stereological/immunohistochemical counts of PV+ and SOM+ interneurons per striatal area in BACHD vs wild-type mice.
findings.effect_size: SOM interneurons 28.1 +/- 4.0 (BACHD) vs 28.8 +/- 2.7 (WT) per unit striatal area, p = 0.4957
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We found that the number of SOM interneurons was not significantly reduced in BACHD mice (BACHD- 28.1 ± 4.0) when compared to wild-type mice (WT- 28.8 ± 2.7, p = 0.4957; Figure 3C).
findings.study_system: BACHD transgenic mouse model of HD; dorsal striatum immunohistochemistry

findings.claim: Increased GABAergic input to striatal cholinergic interneurons in symptomatic R6/2 mice originates from somatostatin-expressing low-threshold spiking interneurons rather than from parvalbumin fast-spiking interneurons.
findings.claim_source_sentence: These results suggest that SOM-positive PLTS interneurons, and not PV-positive FSIs, contribute to the increased GABAergic inputs to LCIs of symptomatic R6/2 mice.
findings.evidence: Cell-type-specific optogenetic activation of SOM-PLTS vs PV-FSI inputs with whole-cell recordings from identified large cholinergic interneurons.
findings.effect_size: 82% of R6/2 cholinergic interneurons responded to SOM-interneuron activation (9/11) vs 62% in WT (8/13)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In LCIs from WT mice (n = 7, age 71 ± 2 d), 62% of cells responded to SOM interneuron activation (8/13) and in LCIs from R6/2 mice (n = 6, age 70 ± 1 d), 82% of cells responded (9/11 cells) (p = 0.27).
findings.study_system: R6/2 transgenic mouse model of HD; striatal large cholinergic interneurons

findings.claim: Parvalbumin interneuron density is markedly reduced in the striatum of vehicle-treated R6/2 mice with somatic atrophy, and PARP-1 inhibition rescues parvalbumin and calretinin interneuron populations.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The density of PARV interneurons was markedly reduced in the vehicle-treated R6/2 mice, with a smaller cell body and fewer or no arborizations.
findings.evidence: Immunohistochemical quantification of PARV and CALR interneurons in R6/2 striatum with and without the PARP-1 inhibitor INO-1001.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: marked reduction in PARV interneuron density with smaller somata and reduced arborization
findings.study_system: R6/2 transgenic mouse model of HD; striatal interneuron immunohistochemistry

findings.claim: In R6/2 cortex, somatostatin- and VIP-expressing interneuron densities decline progressively while parvalbumin interneuron density is unchanged, with somatic shrinkage across all three types.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Our findings in the anterior cingulate cortex were overall similar to the primary motor cortex, with unchanged density of PV+ cells and reduced density of SST+ and VIP+ cells (Figures 2A–F).
findings.evidence: Immunohistochemical density and soma-size quantification of PV+, SST+ and VIP+ interneurons in primary motor and anterior cingulate cortex of R6/2 mice across ages.
findings.effect_size: cell body size reduced by 15% (PV), 16% (SST) and 13% (VIP)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Cell body size of PV, SST, and VIP interneurons was also reduced by 15, 16, and 13%, respectively (Figures 5C–H).
findings.study_system: R6/2 transgenic mouse model of HD; primary motor and anterior cingulate cortex

findings.claim: Striatal cholinergic interneurons in R6/2 mice are relatively resistant to cell loss compared with spiny projection neurons and parvalbumin interneurons, with reductions appearing only late.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Compared to WT mice, sham-lesioned R6/2 mice show a relative resistance to cholinergic neuron loss compared to MSNs or PV+ interneurons, with detectable reduction in numbers occurring at 13 wks, but not at 11 wks (Fig. 3e, w (25) = 0.982, p = 0.92, F(GenotypeXLesion)2,19 = 5.81, p = 0.01, post hoc: WT sham vs 13 wks R6/2 sham p = 0.0005; 11 wks R6/2 sham vs 13 wks R6/2 sham p = 0.005).
findings.evidence: Stereological counts of cholinergic, PV+ interneurons and MSNs in sham- and thalamic-lesioned R6/2 and WT mice.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: relative resistance to cholinergic neuron loss with detectable reduction only at later stages
findings.study_system: R6/2 transgenic mouse model of HD with thalamostriatal lesions; dorsal striatum

findings.claim: Transgenic HD monkeys show major loss of striatal parvalbumin interneurons, establishing interneuron vulnerability in a primate model.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Both HD monkeys displayed a major loss of PV+ neurons in the caudate nucleus compared to control. rHD1 had 46% and 79% fewer PV+ cells in the caudate head and body, respectively, while the same regions contained 56% and 75% fewer PV+ neurons than controls in rHD7.
findings.evidence: Design-based stereological counts of interneuron subtypes and total neurons in caudate and putamen of two transgenic HD monkeys versus control.
findings.effect_size: 46% and 79% fewer PV+ cells in caudate head and body of one HD monkey
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Both HD monkeys displayed a major loss of PV+ neurons in the caudate nucleus compared to control. rHD1 had 46% and 79% fewer PV+ cells in the caudate head and body, respectively, while the same regions contained 56% and 75% fewer PV+ neurons than controls in rHD7.
findings.study_system: Transgenic HD rhesus macaque (nonhuman primate) striatum

findings.claim: GABA-A receptor subunit expression is remodelled cell-type-specifically in HD mice, with alpha1 decreased on striatal parvalbumin interneurons while increased in spiny projection neurons.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This quantitative analysis showed that a significant decrease in α1 subunit expression (83.8 ± 5.4% compared to WT PV cells) had indeed occurred on the somata of striatal PV positive interneurons in 2 month old R6/1 mice (Figure 6F).
findings.evidence: Quantitative immunohistochemistry of GABA-A receptor subunits on identified striatal cell types in HD mouse models.
findings.effect_size: alpha1 subunit expression on PV interneuron somata 83.8 +/- 5.4% of WT
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: This quantitative analysis showed that a significant decrease in α1 subunit expression (83.8 ± 5.4% compared to WT PV cells) had indeed occurred on the somata of striatal PV positive interneurons in 2 month old R6/1 mice (Figure 6F).
findings.study_system: Mouse models of HD (R6/2 and knock-in); striatal interneurons and MSNs

findings.claim: Cre-mediated reduction of mutant huntingtin selectively in somatostatin interneurons normalized their elevated spontaneous firing in BACHD mice, indicating cell-autonomous mHTT effects on SST interneuron physiology.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We found that reduction of mHTT in striatal SST-INs can reduce the observed increased firing in BACHD mice (Fig. 5C).
findings.evidence: Conditional mHTT reduction in SST-Cre;BACHD mice with cell-attached and whole-cell recordings from identified striatal SST interneurons plus behavioural testing.
findings.effect_size: spontaneous firing rate of SST-INs in BACHD/SST-Cre mice not different from control (P=0.9468)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Interestingly, in BACHD/SST-Cre mice, the spontaneous firing rate of SST-INs was not significantly different from that in the control group (P=0.9468) (Fig. 5B,C), suggesting that reducing mHTT expression in striatal SST-INs is sufficient to normalize their intrinsic activity in a cell-autonomous way.
findings.study_system: BACHD x SST-Cre mouse; striatal SST interneurons

findings.claim: R6/2 mice show only small losses of striatal bNOS- and somatostatin-positive interneurons, quantifying the relative (but not absolute) preservation of this population.
findings.claim_source_sentence: R6/2 transgenic mice exhibited 14 and 8% loss of bNOS and SST positive neurons, respectively.
findings.evidence: Immunohistochemical counts of bNOS- and SST-positive striatal neurons in R6/2, SSTR1/5 double knockout and wild-type mice.
findings.effect_size: 14% loss of bNOS-positive and 8% loss of SST-positive neurons in R6/2
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: R6/2 transgenic mice exhibited 14 and 8% loss of bNOS and SST positive neurons, respectively.
findings.study_system: R6/2 transgenic mice and somatostatin receptor 1/5 double knockout mice; striatum

findings.claim: Quinolinic acid lesions of rat striatum significantly reduced parvalbumin- and NPY-positive interneuron numbers, showing that the classical excitotoxic HD model does not spare all interneuron classes.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The numbers of Parv+ interneurons (F = 40.717, df1 = 2, df2 = 12, p<0.01; Fig. 3B; Fig. 5A and B) and NPY+ interneurons (F = 22.846, df1 = 2, df2 = 12, p<0.01; Fig. 3B; Fig. 6A and B) were significantly reduced in the QA group in comparison to the control group.
findings.evidence: Stereological counts and morphometry of Parv+, calretinin+ and NPY+ interneurons after intrastriatal quinolinic acid injection in rats.
findings.effect_size: Parv+ F = 40.717, p<0.01 and NPY+ F = 22.846, p<0.01 versus control
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The numbers of Parv+ interneurons (F = 40.717, df1 = 2, df2 = 12, p<0.01; Fig. 3B; Fig. 5A and B) and NPY+ interneurons (F = 22.846, df1 = 2, df2 = 12, p<0.01; Fig. 3B; Fig. 6A and B) were significantly reduced in the QA group in comparison to the control group.
findings.study_system: Rat quinolinic acid excitotoxic model of HD; striatum

findings.claim: Cortical somatostatin interneuron numbers are reduced in BACHD mice while parvalbumin interneuron numbers are preserved at the same stage, and the deficit traces to aberrant medial ganglionic eminence neurogenesis.
findings.claim_source_sentence: At this stage, the BACHD cortex exhibited a significant reduction in SST+ interneurons compared to controls (Control: 203.4 ± 9.8, n = 10; BACHD: 167.6 ± 9.2, n = 10; t18 = 2.67, p = 0.0157; Fig. 4A/A’,D), whereas PV+ interneuron numbers were not significantly different (Control: 353.1 ± 11.8, n = 10; BACHD: 320.4 ± 14.3, n = 10; t18 = 1.767, p = 0.094; Fig. 4B/B′,E).
findings.evidence: Interneuron counts in BACHD cortex combined with analysis of Lhx6+/Satb1+ MGE progenitors during development.
findings.effect_size: SST+ interneurons: control 203.4 +/- 9.8 vs BACHD 167.6 +/- 9.2 (p = 0.0157); PV+ not different (p = 0.094)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: At this stage, the BACHD cortex exhibited a significant reduction in SST+ interneurons compared to controls (Control: 203.4 ± 9.8, n = 10; BACHD: 167.6 ± 9.2, n = 10; t18 = 2.67, p = 0.0157; Fig. 4A/A’,D), whereas PV+ interneuron numbers were not significantly different (Control: 353.1 ± 11.8, n = 10; BACHD: 320.4 ± 14.3, n = 10; t18 = 1.767, p = 0.094; Fig. 4B/B′,E).
findings.study_system: BACHD mouse model of HD; cortex and medial ganglionic eminence development

findings.claim: Cannabinoid CB1 receptor loss in R6/1 mice is concentrated in hippocampal GABAergic interneurons and underlies impaired depolarization-induced suppression of inhibition; restoring interneuronal CB1R rescues memory deficits.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Notably, the reduction of CB1R protein level in R6/1 mice was predominantly observed in hippocampal GABAergic interneurons, likely accounting for the impaired DSI response.
findings.evidence: Cell-type-specific CB1R quantification and rescue in hippocampal GABAergic neurons of R6/1 mice with electrophysiology and behaviour.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: CB1R protein reduction predominantly in hippocampal GABAergic interneurons
findings.study_system: R6/1 transgenic mouse model of HD; hippocampal GABAergic interneurons

findings.claim: In vivo c-Fos mapping in R6/1 striatum detected activation in parvalbumin interneurons but negligible (<1%) activation among calretinin-, cholinergic- and nNOS-expressing interneurons, leaving the SST/NOS class unassessable by this activity marker.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Only negligible proportions (<1%) were c-Fos+ among Calr-, ChAT-, and nNOS-expressing INs such that no further analysis could have been performed (Fig 7D, Table 4).
findings.evidence: Immediate-early-gene (c-Fos) mapping combined with interneuron markers in dorsomedial striatum of R6/1 and WT mice at pre- and symptomatic ages.
findings.effect_size: <1% of Calr-, ChAT- and nNOS-expressing interneurons were c-Fos positive
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Only negligible proportions (<1%) were c-Fos+ among Calr-, ChAT-, and nNOS-expressing INs such that no further analysis could have been performed (Fig 7D, Table 4).
findings.study_system: R6/1 transgenic mouse model of HD; dorsomedial striatum

findings.claim: Human HD striatal organoids show selective depletion of lateral ganglionic eminence progenitors and medium spiny neurons, recapitulating projection-neuron-selective vulnerability in a human model.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We found that the numbers of LGE progenitor cells (GSH2) and MSNs (DARPP32, CTIP2) were significantly lower in HD striatal organoids (GSH2: 48.45% ± 2.36% vs 32.15% ± 2.76%; DARPP32: 41.10% ± 1.58% vs 20.04% ± 1.38%; CTIP2: 61.56% ± 2.47% vs 44.79% ± 2.09%;) (Fig. 2 B and C).
findings.evidence: Human iPSC-derived striato-nigral assembloids from HD and control lines with immunostaining and single-cell profiling of progenitor and MSN markers.
findings.effect_size: GSH2+ progenitors 48.45% +/- 2.36% (control) vs 32.15% +/- 2.76% (HD)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We found that the numbers of LGE progenitor cells (GSH2) and MSNs (DARPP32, CTIP2) were significantly lower in HD striatal organoids (GSH2: 48.45% ± 2.36% vs 32.15% ± 2.76%; DARPP32: 41.10% ± 1.58% vs 20.04% ± 1.38%; CTIP2: 61.56% ± 2.47% vs 44.79% ± 2.09%;) (Fig. 2 B and C).
findings.study_system: Human HD iPSC-derived striatal organoids/assembloids

findings.claim: Lowering mutant huntingtin selectively in striatal cholinergic interneurons normalized elevated intratelencephalic corticostriatal transmission, whereas lowering it in cortex or in indirect-pathway SPNs did not, localizing the circuit defect to an interneuron class that is not lost in HD.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Indeed, reduction in mHtt selectively in ChIs with viral delivery of zinc finger proteins (ZFPs)31 normalized corticostriatal synaptic transmission, but lowering mHtt in M1 cortex or in iSPNs did not.
findings.evidence: Cell-type-targeted mHtt-lowering zinc-finger proteins combined with optogenetic interrogation of IT and PT corticostriatal inputs in zQ175+/- mice.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: normalization of corticostriatal synaptic transmission after ChI-selective mHtt lowering only
findings.study_system: zQ175 heterozygous knock-in mouse model of HD; dorsal striatum

findings.claim: Presymptomatic chemogenetic manipulation of parvalbumin interneurons, like manipulation of pyramidal neurons, reduced behavioural deficits in R6/2 mice, implicating interneuron circuit dysfunction in symptom expression.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Manipulating either PYR neurons in Emx-Cre x R6/2 mice or PV interneurons in Pv-Cre x R6/2 mice led to a reduction of deficits observed in untreated R6/2 mice.
findings.evidence: Cell-type-specific chemogenetic (DREADD) manipulation in Emx-Cre x R6/2 and Pv-Cre x R6/2 mice with in vivo electrophysiology and behaviour.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: reduction of behavioural deficits relative to untreated R6/2
findings.study_system: R6/2 transgenic mouse crossed to Emx-Cre or Pv-Cre; cortex and striatum

findings.claim: At 12 months in Q175 heterozygous mice, direct-pathway D1 spiny projection neurons show significant structural and functional alterations while D2 neurons are comparatively less affected, indicating differential vulnerability even among projection neurons.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, our results indicate that while the structural and functional properties of D1 MSNs were significantly altered, D2 MSNs were comparatively less affected in the dorsolateral striatum of aged Q175+/- mice.
findings.evidence: Whole-cell recordings and morphological reconstruction of identified D1 and D2 MSNs in dorsolateral striatum of 12-month Q175+/- mice.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: rheobase significantly reduced in Q175 D1 MSNs but unchanged in D2 MSNs
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Rheobase was significantly reduced in D1 MSNs in Q175+/- compared to WT D1 MSNs, while Q175+/- D2 MSNs did not differ from WT D2 MSNs (p-values for post hoc t-tests in Table 2).
findings.study_system: Q175+/- knock-in mouse model of HD; dorsolateral striatum D1 and D2 MSNs

findings.claim: Single-nuclei RNA-seq of an ovine HD model shows altered cell-cell signalling probability across all striatal neuron classes including NPY/SST and cholinergic interneurons, alongside an MSN glutamate excitotoxicity signature.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The communication probability was greater in the OVT73 dataset for all neuronal cells (D1, D2, eccentric MSNs and PV/Th, NPY/SST, cholinergic interneurons), OPCs and astrocytes indicating more cell–cell crosstalk in the OVT73 cell state (Fig. 4A and B, thicker lines indicate higher number of ligand receptor interactions or higher communication probability in OVT73).
findings.evidence: Single-nuclei RNA sequencing of striatum from the OVT73 transgenic sheep HD model with cell-type annotation and cell-cell communication analysis.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: greater communication probability in OVT73 for D1, D2, eccentric MSNs, PV/Th, NPY/SST and cholinergic interneurons
findings.study_system: OVT73 transgenic sheep model of HD; striatum single-nuclei transcriptomes

findings.claim: Optogenetic activation of indirect-pathway SPN collaterals evokes significantly larger IPSCs in cholinergic interneurons of zQ175 mice, while direct-pathway collateral input is unchanged.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Optogenetic activation of iSPN collaterals in ex vivo brain slices from 6 to 7 month-old Adora2-cre X zQ175+/− mice yielded significantly larger evoked inhibitory postsynaptic currents (eIPSCs) than in slices from age-matched, wildtype littermate controls (Figure 1b).
findings.evidence: Ex vivo electrophysiology with pathway-specific optogenetic activation of dSPN and iSPN collaterals onto cholinergic interneurons in zQ175+/- mice.
findings.effect_size: significantly larger evoked IPSCs in zQ175 cholinergic interneurons upon iSPN collateral activation
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Optogenetic activation of iSPN collaterals in ex vivo brain slices from 6 to 7 month-old Adora2-cre X zQ175+/− mice yielded significantly larger evoked inhibitory postsynaptic currents (eIPSCs) than in slices from age-matched, wildtype littermate controls (Figure 1b).
findings.study_system: zQ175+/- knock-in mouse model of HD; striatal cholinergic interneurons

findings.claim: Conditional loss of huntingtin in subpallial (MGE/LGE) lineages produces early deficits of somatostatin-positive and Reelin-positive interneurons with increased cholinergic interneurons, showing that wild-type huntingtin function is required for normal interneuron development.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Furthermore, we observed early deficits of somatostatin-positive and Reelin-positive interneurons in both Htt subpallial null strains, as well as early increases of cholinergic interneurons, Foxp2 + arkypallidal neurons, and incipient deficits with age-dependent loss of parvalbumin-positive neurons in Htt flx ;Nkx2.1-Cre mice.
findings.evidence: Conditional Htt deletion in Gsx2-Cre and Nkx2.1-Cre lineages with interneuron marker quantification and behavioural phenotyping.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: early deficits of SST+ and Reelin+ interneurons; early increases of cholinergic interneurons
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Furthermore, we observed early deficits of somatostatin-positive and Reelin-positive interneurons in both Htt subpallial null strains, as well as early increases of cholinergic interneurons, Foxp2 + arkypallidal neurons, and incipient deficits with age-dependent loss of parvalbumin-positive neurons in Htt flx ;Nkx2.1-Cre mice.
findings.study_system: Htt-flox x Gsx2-Cre and Htt-flox x Nkx2.1-Cre mice; striatum and cortex

findings.claim: In Q175 mice the basic membrane and synaptic properties of low-threshold spiking (SST/NOS) interneurons are unchanged across disease stages, whereas fast-spiking interneurons show altered morphology and function.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The basic membrane and synaptic properties of LTS interneurons were similar in Q175 and WT mice regardless of disease stage.
findings.evidence: Side-by-side morphological and whole-cell electrophysiological comparison of FSIs and LTS interneurons in Q175 and WT striatum at presymptomatic and symptomatic ages.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: LTS interneuron membrane and synaptic properties similar in Q175 and WT at all stages
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The basic membrane and synaptic properties of LTS interneurons were similar in Q175 and WT mice regardless of disease stage.
findings.study_system: Q175 knock-in mouse model of HD; striatal FSI and LTS interneurons

findings.claim: Cannabinoid CB1 receptor expression is downregulated in striatal NPY/nNOS-expressing interneurons across two mouse models and in human HD caudate, showing molecular pathology in a population that survives.
findings.claim_source_sentence: CB(1) downregulation in striatal NPY/nNOS-expressing interneurons occurs in R6/2 mice, Hdh(Q150/Q150) mice and the caudate nucleus of patients with HD.
findings.evidence: Unbiased semi-quantitative immunohistochemistry for CB1 in identified interneuron populations in R6/2 and Hdh(Q150) mice and human HD caudate nucleus.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: CB1 downregulation in NPY/nNOS interneurons in R6/2, Hdh(Q150/Q150) and human HD caudate
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: CB(1) downregulation in striatal NPY/nNOS-expressing interneurons occurs in R6/2 mice, Hdh(Q150/Q150) mice and the caudate nucleus of patients with HD.
findings.study_system: R6/2 and Hdh(Q150/Q150) mice and human HD post-mortem caudate nucleus

findings.claim: Restricting mutant huntingtin expression to parvalbumin-positive neurons is sufficient to produce hyperactivity and cortical disinhibition with impaired GABA release, demonstrating cell-autonomous interneuron pathology.
findings.claim_source_sentence: At midlife, mutant mice are hyperactive and display impaired GABA release in the motor cortex, characterized by reduced miniature inhibitory events and severely blunted responses to gamma frequency stimulation, without a loss of PV-positive interneurons.
findings.evidence: Cre-lox restricted expression of mutant huntingtin in PV-positive neurons with cortical electrophysiology and behavioural assessment.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: reduced miniature inhibitory events and blunted gamma-frequency responses in motor cortex
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: At midlife, mutant mice are hyperactive and display impaired GABA release in the motor cortex, characterized by reduced miniature inhibitory events and severely blunted responses to gamma frequency stimulation, without a loss of PV-positive interneurons.
findings.study_system: PV-Cre driven mutant huntingtin mouse; motor cortex and behaviour

findings.claim: Neuronal nitric oxide synthase mRNA is significantly decreased in HD caudate and putamen but not in sensorimotor cortex, indicating molecular downregulation within the supposedly spared NOS/SST/NPY interneuron population.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Neuronal nitric oxide synthase messenger RNA was significantly decreased in the caudate nucleus and putamen, but not in the sensorimotor cortex in Huntington's disease; the decrease in neuronal nitric oxide synthase messenger RNA became more pronounced with the severity of the disease.
findings.evidence: In situ hybridization quantification of nNOS and somatostatin mRNA in post-mortem HD and control caudate, putamen and sensorimotor cortex.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: significant decrease of nNOS mRNA in caudate nucleus and putamen but not sensorimotor cortex
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Neuronal nitric oxide synthase messenger RNA was significantly decreased in the caudate nucleus and putamen, but not in the sensorimotor cortex in Huntington's disease; the decrease in neuronal nitric oxide synthase messenger RNA became more pronounced with the severity of the disease.
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem HD brain (caudate, putamen, sensorimotor cortex)

findings.claim: Cortical GABAergic interneuron loss in human HD is region- and symptom-specific: the anterior cingulate cortex loses calbindin, calretinin and parvalbumin interneurons severely, while the primary motor cortex loses only calbindin interneurons in motor-dominant cases.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In contrast, the anterior cingulate cortex showed a major significant loss in all 3 interneuron populations, with 71% loss of calbindin (p=0.001), 60% loss of calretinin (p=0.001), and 80% loss of parvalbumin interneurons (p=0.005) in HD cases with major mood disorder, and no interneuron loss was observed in cases with major motor dysfunction.
findings.evidence: Double-blind stereological counts of calbindin-D28k, calretinin and parvalbumin interneurons in primary motor and anterior cingulate cortex of symptom-stratified human HD cases.
findings.effect_size: 71% loss of calbindin (p=0.001), 60% loss of calretinin (p=0.001) and 80% loss of parvalbumin interneurons in anterior cingulate cortex
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In contrast, the anterior cingulate cortex showed a major significant loss in all 3 interneuron populations, with 71% loss of calbindin (p=0.001), 60% loss of calretinin (p=0.001), and 80% loss of parvalbumin interneurons (p=0.005) in HD cases with major mood disorder, and no interneuron loss was observed in cases with major motor dysfunction.
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem HD cortex stratified by motor vs mood symptom dominance

findings.claim: Huntingtin immunoreactivity accumulates in striatal projection neurons while cholinergic, parvalbumin, calretinin and nNOS interneurons show little or no huntingtin immunoreactivity, offering a protein-expression basis for differential vulnerability.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Striatal interneurons, identified by the presence of immunoreactivity for choline acetyltransferase, parvalbumin, calretinin, or neuronal nitric oxide synthase, exhibit little or no HT-ir.
findings.evidence: Immunohistochemical mapping of huntingtin immunoreactivity across identified projection neuron and interneuron populations in rat neostriatum.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: little or no huntingtin immunoreactivity in ChAT-, parvalbumin-, calretinin- or nNOS-positive interneurons
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Striatal interneurons, identified by the presence of immunoreactivity for choline acetyltransferase, parvalbumin, calretinin, or neuronal nitric oxide synthase, exhibit little or no HT-ir.
findings.study_system: Rat neostriatum; identified projection neurons and interneuron subtypes

findings.claim: Somatostatin and neuropeptide Y concentrations are increased in HD striatum across pathological grades, a pattern consistent with relative but not absolute sparing of the aspiny interneurons that co-express them.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Increases in mild and severe grades were similar, which is consistent with a relative but not absolute sparing of striatal aspiny neurons in which somatostatin and neuropeptide Y are colocalized.

findings.claim: NADPH-diaphorase staining is reduced in the motor cortex of aged male Q175 mice in an age- and sex-dependent manner, indicating late functional decline of the NOS interneuron population.

findings.claim: Somatostatin itself confers the selective resistance of medium-sized aspiny striatal interneurons to NMDA-receptor-mediated excitotoxicity, providing a mechanistic account of their sparing.

arg_unanchored.thesis: The textbook claim that striatal SST/NPY/NOS interneurons are spared in Huntington's disease rests on peptide concentrations measured in atrophic tissue, and the primary authors described relative, not absolute, preservation. subsections.title: The sparing claim and its measurement basis
subsections.job: Reconstruct the provenance of the claim: elevated somatostatin and NPY concentrations in HD basal ganglia, NADPH-diaphorase histochemistry, and normalisation against atrophic tissue. State plainly that absolute sparing with modern cell-type-specific markers and unbiased stereology was not demonstrated in the retrieved literature - a false-consensus risk.

subsections.title: Peptide up, transcript down: the dissociation inside the spared population
subsections.job: Present in situ hybridisation showing significantly decreased nNOS and somatostatin mRNA in the same region where peptide concentration is elevated, and draw the conclusion the two measures jointly support: surviving cells with downregulated transcription in shrunken tissue.

subsections.title: Sparing relative to what: the parvalbumin contrast
subsections.job: Establish PV as the striatal and cortical interneuron class with the most consistent loss evidence across genetic mouse models, a transgenic primate, excitotoxic rodent lesions and human cortex, and define SST sparing explicitly as relative to that.

subsections.title: Functional pathology in a surviving population
subsections.job: Weigh the electrophysiological disagreement over which interneuron class drives the increased GABAergic drive onto projection neurons - pharmacogenetic silencing implicating SOM cells against paired recording and optogenetics assigning the excess to PV cells - and the model-dependent disagreement over whether SST intrinsic physiology changes at all.

subsections.title: Aggregates, somatic expansion and the failure of burden to predict death
subsections.job: Use the quantitative dissociation: spared NADPH-diaphorase interneurons carry abundant aggregates, direct- and indirect-pathway MSNs expand repeats equally despite unequal vulnerability, and cortical SST interneurons are lost with only modest expansion. Neither aggregate load nor expansion magnitude predicts which cells die.

subsections.title: Cortex versus striatum, mouse versus human
subsections.job: Close on the species and region split: mouse HD models lose cortical SST interneurons while human HD cortex evidence is limited to a spatial-transcriptomic preprint reporting loss and older peptide studies reporting increases; no human stereological SST count in HD cortex was retrieved.

opening_constraint: (sec-parkinsons-lewy-body) showed a striatal peptidergic system responding to dopamine loss without dying; HD asks what happens to the same class when its postsynaptic targets are destroyed around it.
closing_constraint: HD demonstrates that a population can be numerically preserved and functionally abnormal. (sec-als-ftd) shows the opposite evidential problem: a disease group where the cell class is barely measured in human tissue at all, and the mechanistic account rests on a single mouse study.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Somatostatin interneurons in human HD cortex
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Direct stereological or molecular quantification of SST-expressing interneurons in human HD neocortex; published human cortical interneuron counts cover calbindin, calretinin and parvalbumin only, and the SST reduction is documented only in mouse models.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The central claim of cortical SST involvement in HD rests entirely on mouse models, so the human relevance of the cortical SST deficit is untested.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: 'Striatal interneurons are spared in Huntington's disease' (false_consensus_risk)
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration of absolute sparing with modern cell-type-specific markers and unbiased stereology; the claim traces to peptide-concentration and NADPH-diaphorase histochemistry studies whose own authors described relative, not absolute, sparing.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: the sparing claim is repeated as established while the primary data support only relative preservation, and several model studies report 8-14% losses and molecular downregulation within the same population.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Single-cell transcriptomics of SST interneurons in HD
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Human HD single-nucleus datasets with sufficient interneuron depth to test whether SST/NPY/NOS interneurons show cell-autonomous transcriptional pathology; available interneuron-resolved single-nuclei data come from an ovine model.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Without human interneuron-resolved transcriptomes it is impossible to distinguish survival from dysfunction in the population assumed to be spared.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Mechanism of differential vulnerability between spiny projection neurons and SST/NOS interneurons
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Causal tests of the candidate determinants (NMDA receptor paucity, somatostatin itself, optineurin and HAP1 expression, low huntingtin accumulation) in a single preparation; existing evidence is correlational and distributed across preparations and decades.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Differential vulnerability is the central mechanistic question of the cluster, yet no study manipulates a candidate determinant and measures interneuron survival in an HD genetic model.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Electrophysiology of SST interneurons in human HD tissue
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Any direct physiological recording of identified SST interneurons from human HD tissue or human HD-derived interneuron cultures.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: All conclusions about SST interneuron hyperactivity or normality come from mouse models that disagree with one another.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Functional characterisation of spared striatal SST/NOS interneurons in HD
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Sparing is established mainly by cell counts, peptide concentrations and histochemistry; in vivo recordings or activity imaging of identified SST/nNOS striatal interneurons in HD models are almost absent, so 'spared' means 'present', not 'functionally normal'.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Surviving-but-dysfunctional interneurons would change the circuit interpretation of HD striatal pathology and the therapeutic logic of targeting them.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Cell-type-resolved stereology of somatostatin interneurons in human HD cortex
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Quantitative, grade-stratified counts of cortical SST interneurons in human HD using modern cell-resolved methods exist mainly in a single unrefereed preprint; the older human literature measured peptide concentration rather than cell number.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The cortical SST story in HD currently rests on model systems and one preprint, yet it is the key link between HD cortical pathology and interneuron-specific vulnerability.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Primary experimental basis for the claim that NOS/somatostatin interneuron sparing is cell-autonomous
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration - the claim that interneuron sparing reflects intrinsic (cell-autonomous) resistance is repeated across reviews, but conditional mutant-huntingtin experiments restricted to striatal interneuron classes were not identified in these searches.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: widely stated mechanistic claim without a traceable cell-type-restricted genetic experiment.

unreplicated_claims_to_flag.claim: Somatostatin itself is responsible for the selective sparing of medium-sized aspiny striatal interneurons under NMDA-receptor-mediated excitotoxicity
Optineurin is abundantly expressed in striatal interneurons and only weakly in projection neurons, complementary to the HD loss pattern
HAP1 mRNA is co-enriched with nNOS mRNA in discrete neuronal populations, linking huntingtin interactors to the NOS/SST class
Restricting mutant huntingtin to parvalbumin-positive neurons alone suffices to produce cortical disinhibition and hyperactivity
Chandelier and somatostatin-positive cortical interneurons are lost in human HD despite only modest somatic repeat expansion and aggregate load.

Endpoints actually used: Europe PMC REST search (resultType=core) and fullTextXML, NCBI E-utilities efetch (db=pmc), CrossRef. certified_evidence_limits.citation_chasing: None. No backward or forward citation chasing was performed. No section may claim completeness of coverage; write 'no study examining X was retrieved by these searches', never 'no study has examined X'.
certified_evidence_limits.fulltext_shortfall_concentration: The shortfall is concentrated in pre-2000 closed-access postmortem and CSF literature (radioimmunoassay series), which is recorded at abstract level only. Sections whose argument rests on that literature must state the asymmetry in the section body, not only in Methods.
certified_evidence_limits.disconfirming_sweeps: Disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. Negative-result and conflict coverage is a top-relevance sample, not a census. Report null results as 'reported null results include ...'; never as 'no contradicting evidence exists'. No rate of contradiction may be reported as complete.
certified_evidence_limits.conflict_axis_labels_provisional: Axes were assigned by a documented rule applied to the recorded nature_of_conflict text. Five candidate axes (measurement modality and what was counted; species, region and circuit context; model construct and species transfer; cohort composition, stage and comorbidity; design rigor and statistical unit) were keyword-scored, with the region/species axis down-weighted (0.55) because regional context is named in almost every conflict record, and design rigor up-weighted (1.3) because it is named rarely and only when it is the point. Each conflict carries a primary axis and the full set of axes present, since most of these disagreements are genuinely multi-axis. These tags are a planning classification derived from the conflict text, not a measurement; the writing phase should correct any tag that misreads a conflict, and the atlas figure must state that conflicts can appear in more than one axis row.
certified_evidence_limits.conflict_inventory_caveat: This inventory is the set of disagreements recorded during a search whose disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. It is a top-relevance sample of the disagreement in this literature, not a census, and no rate of contradiction may be reported as complete.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Europe PMC-dominant retrieval with no citation chasing (snowball_rounds = 0)
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: No section may claim completeness of coverage. The Methods section states the database scope and the absence of backward/forward citation chasing explicitly. Claims of the form "no study has examined X" are written as "no study examining X was retrieved by these searches", and every such statement in a body section is sourced to a recorded evidence gap rather than asserted.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Full-text share varies from 77/77 (circuits, cluster_07) to 22/87 (human evidence, cluster_08) because the older postmortem and CSF literature is closed-access
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Section 9 is the section whose underlying literature is least directly verified. Its thesis is written so that the central synthesis rests on the modern open-access single-nucleus cohorts, with the 1980s radioimmunoassay series treated as a historically important but abstract-level record; the asymmetry is stated in the section itself, not buried in Methods. Section 5 (25/80 full text) carries the same caveat for its historical CSF series.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query, so negative-result coverage is a top-relevance sample rather than an exhaustive search
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Null results are reported as "reported null results include ..." and never as "no contradicting evidence exists". Section 11 states that the conflict inventory is a sample of the disagreement in this literature, not a census, and that the true rate of unreplicated or contradicted claims is bounded below by what is recorded here.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: cluster_09's replication ceiling (therapeutics) is met by a single enabling label; 60 of 86 findings are replication_unknown
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Section 10 is framed as an assessment of translational status, not of efficacy. No therapeutic claim in that section may be described as replicated unless the specific replicating DOI is named, and the section foregrounds that much of the SSTR4 evidence base comes from one closely related research programme.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Figure comparisons are heterogeneous: no figure_data entry is uniform on all four homogeneity_check fields
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Every figure specification states the heterogeneity it must display rather than smooth, and the document-level figure rules forbid pooled summaries outright.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Several prominent mechanistic claims are flagged as false-consensus risks in the evidence record (metabolic load as the cause of SST vulnerability; SST/GABA co-transmission; absolute sparing of striatal interneurons in HD)
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Each is introduced in prose as a widely repeated claim whose primary demonstration was not retrieved, in sections 3, 2 and 6 respectively, and each is listed in the section 11 open-questions inventory.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: The sparing claim and its measurement basis
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Reconstruct the provenance of the claim: elevated somatostatin and NPY concentrations in HD basal ganglia, NADPH-diaphorase histochemistry, and normalisation against atrophic tissue. State plainly that absolute sparing with modern cell-type-specific markers and unbiased stereology was not demonstrated in the retrieved literature - a false-consensus risk.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Peptide up, transcript down: the dissociation inside the spared population
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Present in situ hybridisation showing significantly decreased nNOS and somatostatin mRNA in the same region where peptide concentration is elevated, and draw the conclusion the two measures jointly support: surviving cells with downregulated transcription in shrunken tissue.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Sparing relative to what: the parvalbumin contrast
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Establish PV as the striatal and cortical interneuron class with the most consistent loss evidence across genetic mouse models, a transgenic primate, excitotoxic rodent lesions and human cortex, and define SST sparing explicitly as relative to that.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Functional pathology in a surviving population
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Weigh the electrophysiological disagreement over which interneuron class drives the increased GABAergic drive onto projection neurons - pharmacogenetic silencing implicating SOM cells against paired recording and optogenetics assigning the excess to PV cells - and the model-dependent disagreement over whether SST intrinsic physiology changes at all.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Aggregates, somatic expansion and the failure of burden to predict death
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Use the quantitative dissociation: spared NADPH-diaphorase interneurons carry abundant aggregates, direct- and indirect-pathway MSNs expand repeats equally despite unequal vulnerability, and cortical SST interneurons are lost with only modest expansion. Neither aggregate load nor expansion magnitude predicts which cells die.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Cortex versus striatum, mouse versus human
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Close on the species and region split: mouse HD models lose cortical SST interneurons while human HD cortex evidence is limited to a spatial-transcriptomic preprint reporting loss and older peptide studies reporting increases; no human stereological SST count in HD cortex was retrieved.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_explains_the_discrepancy: Peptide-concentration measurements indicate increased somatostatin/NPY in HD striatum consistent with sparing of the SST/NPY/NOS population, whereas in situ hybridization shows significantly decreased nNOS and somatostatin mRNA in the same region; the two measures (peptide content normalised to atrophic tissue vs per-neuron transcript level) disagree on whether this interneuron class is functionally intact.

Whether somatostatin-expressing low-threshold-spiking interneurons are a source of the increased GABAergic synaptic activity onto striatal projection neurons in HD: pharmacogenetic silencing experiments attribute a major share of elevated sIPSC frequency to SOM interneurons, whereas paired recording and optogenetic activation of the same class report no genotype difference in evoked MSN responses, with the excess inhibition assigned mainly to PV fast-spiking cells.

Whether somatostatin/NOS interneurons are genuinely spared in HD: spatial transcriptomic cell counting in human HD cortex reports loss of somatostatin-positive and chandelier interneurons, while the canonical striatal neuropathology synthesis holds that NOS/somatostatin interneurons are relatively spared. The disagreement is partly regional (cortex versus striatum) and partly methodological (cell-resolved spatial counting versus peptide markers and histochemistry).

Mouse HD models show progressive loss of cortical SST interneuron density, whereas human HD cortex shows increased somatostatin-like immunoreactivity interpreted as selective sparing of cortical SST/NPY neurons; conflict spans species and measurement type (cell density vs peptide concentration).

Human HD anterior cingulate cortex loses 80% of parvalbumin interneurons, while R6/2 mouse cortex shows unchanged parvalbumin interneuron density with selective reduction of SST and VIP cells; the cortical interneuron subtype that is most vulnerable differs between human tissue and the mouse model.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Not tied to a named figure comparison or a recorded conflict; group into convergent paragraphs of 5-8 citations each rather than covering sequentially.

curation_notes.assignment_rule: Deterministic cluster->section mapping from gate_scope.json cluster_to_section_assignment, applied to unique (doi, claim_source_sentence) evidence units.
curation_notes.bookend_rule: Sections 01 and 12 are bookends written at Phase 11 and may cite only papers already used in body sections. Each bookend finding is a Phase 2 finding whose DOI also carries a different finding, with a different claim_source_sentence, in a body section - so the paper is already in the body and the two sections quote different sentences.
curation_notes.duplicate_policy: 35 of 844 Phase 2 findings were byte-identical (same DOI and same claim_source_sentence) records of the same observation in two or more clusters. They were merged into the surviving finding object (also_recorded_in_clusters / duplicate_finding_ids_merged) and logged in unassigned_findings.json; none were deleted.
curation_notes.conflict_axis_caveat: AXIS labels on conflicts are rule-derived and provisional (scaffold conflict_coverage.axis_assignment_method). Correct any tag that misreads a conflict.
curation_notes.citation_discipline: Papers in this package come only from Phase 2 outputs. Do not introduce new citations; cite_keys are from the certified citation_key_map and author names only from author_name_table.
